name: Saint Robert Bellarmine
history: A Jesuit theologian and cardinal from Montepulciano, the foremost defender of Catholic teaching in the controversies after the Reformation. His catechisms taught children for three centuries. He lived poorly, gave freely to the poor, and guided the young Aloysius Gonzaga. He was canonised in 1930 and named a Doctor of the Church a year later.
life: Robert Bellarmine was born in 1542, a nephew of Pope Marcellus II, and entered the Jesuits in 1560. Small, often unwell and quick-witted, he taught first at Louvain and then at the Roman College, where his lectures became the Controversies, a vast and careful statement of Catholic teaching on the questions disputed with the Reformers. He was known for setting out his opponents’ arguments fairly. Clement VIII made him a cardinal in 1599, and he served for three years as archbishop of Capua. In 1616 he was involved in the Church’s first inquiry into Galileo’s teaching. In Rome he kept a simple household, gave away most of his income, and wrote short spiritual books, among them The Art of Dying Well. He died in 1621, asking to be laid near Aloysius Gonzaga, whose confessor he had been; they now rest close together in Sant’Ignazio.
prayerTo: Saint Robert, you served the truth with learning, patience and courtesy, and lived simply among the riches of Rome. Pray for teachers of the faith and for all who seek the truth in good conscience, and for me, that I may know my faith well, speak of it with charity, and prepare each day to die well. Amen.
penance: Read a page of the Catechism today, and give away something of which you have more than you need.
meditation: Bellarmine taught that the art of dying well is learned by living well. If today were your last, what would you want to put right?
